sources.title: Chen Yanliang: Monetary changes under Liang and Chen, Tsing Hua Journal 42(4), 2012
sources.note: Original publisher abstract read, and printed p. 689 read in full through indexed original PDF; direct PDF timed out. Reproducible query: site.thjcs.site.nthu.edu.tw/var/file/452/1452/img/1577/284730408.pdf 大貨六銖 十一年. Article pp. 657-697. Quotes Sui shu 24 for grain/silk and exchange-rate changes; same-work derived budget considered conservatively alongside Sui shu medical passage.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of American History: Tai Huo Liu Zhu, China, 579
sources.note: Full indexed museum record read via exact query nmah_1942599; duplicate si.edu institutional record independently indexed. Direct opens intermittently fail. Accession NU.66.12812, not a separately catalogued facsimile. Museum gives 579, copper, 1 by 25 mm, seal script, 太货六铢 / TAI HUO LIU ZHU / Large Coin Six Zhu. Traditional modern-type normalization and tonal modern Mandarin are editorial.

sources.title: Book of Chen, juan 33: Confucian scholars
sources.note: Transmitted primary history compiled under Tang; modern typeset transcription read directly. Shen Zhu mourning ruling, Zheng Zhuo copying and melon anecdote, Zhang Ji garden teaching. Anecdotes are attributed to this later account and career spans across Liang/Chen retained. Whole-work budget combined for all passages.

sources.title: Book of Sui, juan 78: Xu Zhizang
sources.note: Directly read modern typeset primary transcription, Xu Zhizang paragraph: grandfather Daoyou studies medicine for his mother, intergenerational teaching, Chen service and later Sui appointment. Miraculous dream, diagnostic certainty and claims of universal cure omitted. Same-work total includes money passage indirectly drawing on juan 24, conservatively checked.

sources.title: Hunan University Yuelu Academy: Wei Zheng on identifying Chen tombs
sources.note: Original university report by Zhang Ke and Huang Hexi of Wei Zheng’s 9 December 2024 lecture, published 16 December, read in full. Huang Faqu inscription dates 576. Lingshan royal attribution and migration/art diffusion are clearly the scholar’s interpretations; no settled imperial identification claimed.

sources.title: Zhonghua Shuju editors explain the revised Book of Chen
sources.note: Gao Dan’s original interview/report, 10 September 2021, full text read. Editors Xu Jun, Sun Wenying and Li Mian describe compilation and epitaph/text comparison. Dates 557 and 589 and 2021 editorial work directly stated.

sources.title: Zhao Runyu and Sun Qi: Treatment of Jiankang after the Sui conquest of Chen
sources.note: Original journal Chinese and English abstracts read directly, Taishan University Journal 47(1), 2025, pp. 15-21. Full article not accessed. Uses only abstract’s sequence: destructive initial policy and intended relocation, rebellion, changed policy, retained civilian housing/markets and administrative continuity.

proposedOverrides.name: Chen dynasty
proposedOverrides.summary: The last Southern Dynasty, based at Jiankang, historically 557-589; its imported polygon overstates its changing territory.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record only. No association with Southern Qi, Liang, Sui, ancient Chen state or Vietnamese Tran dynasty. Index 557-589 is historically appropriate; border feature instead runs 557-600.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: Decoded HB world-500.json polygon bbox [99.75159751597516,17.664716126236726,122.39222392223922,37.949767193223835], identical to Southern Qi feature bbox and oversized inherited outline. Public overview flags broad reach and erroneous continuation. Detailed record in identity.json.
batchIdentityNotes.dateDecision: Override retains indexed 557-589; periods 557-569,569-582,582-589. No midpoint dates invented for archaeological interpretations or scholars’ undated habits. Emperor Shubao accession is 582, not first full Zhide era year 583.
batchIdentityNotes.writingDecision: Authentic museum coin dated 579, object NU.66.12812. Exact catalogue simplified Chinese 太货六铢 rendered in modern traditional type 太貨六銖; modern Mandarin pinyin and museum translation explicitly contextualized. Not a facsimile or surviving manuscript claim.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Lingshan imperial attribution and art/migration link are interpretations attributed to Wei Zheng. Scholar anecdotes are later Book of Chen recollections; no universal family diet, schooling, medical or sanitation system inferred. Monetary details indirectly quote Sui shu 24; conservative same-work total combined with medical passage.
